example: Move your own car and gently answer “brr”.
Join the movement. You do not ask for another sound.
steps: Watch for a safe action or comfortable sound to join.
Copy it once with your own toy or action, without mocking.
Pause to see whether your child wants another turn. Their turn can be an action.
If it stays enjoyable, continue briefly. A natural word such as “go” can fit, but you do not need a sound-to-word drill.
responses: A point or gesture
Copy or answer the safe action. Gestures are full turns in this game.
An unclear word or sound
Answer a playful sound warmly without grading its accuracy. Do not teach a specific speech sound through repeated attempts.
No reply
Join the movement quietly or stop. Copying you is optional.
No or turning away
Stop your imitation. Some children do not enjoy being copied.
Frustration
Lower the sound, stop and offer comfort. Do not continue to get a turn.
activities.easier: Use a silent safe action with your own object, or just watch.
activities.ending: “All done.” Let the game end without a final imitation.
activities.vary: If enjoyed, join a different child-led safe action another day. This is interaction, not treatment for a speech-sound difficulty.

activities.title: A toy goes to sleep
activities.goal: Offer one simple pretend action with clear language.
activities.materials: A familiar stuffed toy and a small cloth used only for the toy, kept away from faces. No covering a child or enclosed spaces.
activities.setup: Try this only if pretend play is interesting. Other safe play is equally welcome; this is not a developmental test.
example: Lay your toy on its side: “Bear’s sleeping.”
Says “bear” and stands the toy up.
Follow that change rather than insist on the bedtime story.
steps: Offer one sleeping action with your own toy.
Watch whether your child joins or changes the action.
Describe the action they choose using a short phrase.
Leave room for their turn. You do not need to ask “What is bear doing?”
responses: A point or gesture
If they indicate the toy or move it, respond to that movement with a fitting comment.
An unclear word or sound
If they say a version of bear, answer with its name or a brief action phrase without correcting the sound.
No reply
Keep the action brief or let them explore. No pretend or spoken response is required.
No or turning away
Follow a different safe interest or put the toy aside.
Frustration
Remove the cloth or toy if needed and offer comfort. Do not insist on finishing the pretend sequence.
activities.easier: Use only the toy and one action; skip the cloth and any story.
activities.ending: “Finished.” Put your toy down when the child is done.
activities.vary: If enjoyed later, let another toy sleep using the same simple language.

activities.title: Put familiar things in a basket
activities.goal: Use a place or description word during a shared routine.
activities.materials: A light open basket and a few clean safe clothes or large toys. No cords, detergent, heavy lids or small parts.
activities.setup: Let your child join an ordinary tidy-up if interested. You can model the action yourself; do not require them to sort correctly.
example: Put your shirt in: “In the basket.”
Continue kindly. The purpose is sharing meaning, not correct placement.
steps: Choose a couple of familiar safe items.
Describe one action or item as it becomes relevant.
If your child hands something to you, acknowledge and use it.
Do the practical tidying yourself where needed. A shared comment can be enough.
responses: A point or gesture
If they show you an item, name or describe it. Showing is a message, not a failed request.
An unclear word or sound
If they use part of a familiar name, respond to the meaning. If uncertain, look at the item together.
No reply
Continue your own action without asking for a label.
No or turning away
Let them stop joining. Do not make leaving depend on saying “finished”.
Frustration
Put down the task and attend to the need; tidy later if practical.
activities.easier: Use one item and one comment, with the adult doing all the placing.
activities.ending: “All done.” Finish without counting successful turns.
activities.vary: Another day, use the same “in” meaning with the open toy box.

activities.title: Look together through a window
activities.goal: Share an interest with a comment instead of a naming quiz.
activities.materials: A safe indoor view through a closed or secured window. Follow usual window safety; no climbing or roadside observation task.
activities.setup: Join only when your child notices something. You do not need to find a set number of things.
example: Points at a bus outside and says “bus”.
“It’s gone.” Pause and enjoy looking together.
steps: Notice what catches your child’s interest from a safe position.
Say one comment about it rather than “What is that?”
Respond to their point, sound or word. Add one idea only if it fits.
Stay with the view or move on when they do. No naming test is needed.
responses: A point or gesture
Follow the direction of the point and comment. If unsure what they mean, look together.
An unclear word or sound
If a sound seems to name the bus, answer “Bus!” without asking for clearer speech.
No reply
Watch together quietly. You can share attention without a spoken answer or eye contact.
No or turning away
Move on; do not hold them at the window to complete the activity.
Frustration
Attend to comfort and leave the spot. Stop the parent-practice task.
activities.easier: One shared look and one comment is enough.
activities.ending: “Gone” if the object leaves, or “All done” when you move away.
activities.vary: Use a similar comment for a bus picture later if it interests your child.
